# Routes Gozar offers for Dalan

<!-- Generated by scripts/routes-doc.mjs from the installed Gozar registry. Do not edit; run `node scripts/routes-doc.mjs` to refresh. -->

Dalan needs one Gozar route to publish its address. This page lists the routes in the Gozar release Dalan bundles, as Gozar describes them. Pick one with `--route <id>`:

```bash
dalan routes                              # what Gozar offers on this computer, and whether each route is usable now
dalan service install --worker NAME --route <id>
dalan try --public --route <id>
```

Whether a route is usable depends on your computer and accounts, so `dalan routes` is the check that counts. This page does not say which route to choose.

## Cloudflare named tunnel

- Id: `cloudflare-named` (use `--route cloudflare-named`)
- Cloudflare named tunnel: reaches internet clients, stable address, Cloudflare lists a $0 Free Zero Trust plan with connector software included, but no page names Cloudflare Tunnel.
- Needs: Needs a Cloudflare account and an existing named tunnel. This route is not available in this release.
- Reach: internet; transport: https; lifetimes: none
- Address: stable (hostname route in the owner’s Cloudflare account; no admitted create recipe; DNS and the tunnel are owner-managed prerequisites); public ports: assigned by the provider
- Proof before publishing: checked from public; checks: tls, nonce, sse
- Traffic: readers Cloudflare edge; provider can read payload: yes; TLS ends at: provider
- Cost: Cloudflare lists a $0 Free Zero Trust plan with connector software included, but no page names Cloudflare Tunnel.; account needed: yes
- Consent text: Cloudflare named tunnel is detected only. Gozar cannot create a route with it yet. The Cloudflare edge terminates TLS and can read payloads.
  - Terms: https://www.cloudflare.com/terms/
  - Privacy: https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/

## Local network

- Id: `lan` (use `--route lan`)
- Local network: reaches lan clients, unknown address, Gozar charges nothing and there is no provider; the owned local forwarder uses your own network.
- Needs: Needs a network address on this computer that other devices on the same network can reach. Traffic is not encrypted.
- Reach: lan; transport: http; lifetimes: session
- Address: unknown (selected interface address with an OS-assigned port; firewall and routing are the owner’s prerequisites; no TLS: HTTPS-required clients cannot use it); public ports: assigned by the provider
- Proof before publishing: checked from lan; checks: tls, nonce, sse
- Traffic: readers the local network path (unencrypted HTTP); provider can read payload: no; TLS ends at: unknown
- Cost: Gozar charges nothing and there is no provider; the owned local forwarder uses your own network.; account needed: no
- Consent text: Expose this service on a selected local network interface over plain HTTP through an owned forwarder. Anyone on that network path can read the traffic.

## localhost.run trial

- Id: `localhost-run` (use `--route localhost-run`)
- localhost.run trial: reaches internet clients, ephemeral address, The free tier costs nothing and needs no signup; its domains change regularly and have a speed limit.
- Needs: Needs the ssh command on this computer and outbound internet access. No account is needed.
- Reach: internet; transport: https; lifetimes: session
- Address: ephemeral (random hostname under lhr.life for one connection; trial: uptime and URL lifetime are not guaranteed; a new connection gets a new URL; the plan limits a session to 15 minutes); public ports: assigned by the provider
- Proof before publishing: checked from public; checks: tls, nonce, sse
- Traffic: readers localhost.run relay; provider can read payload: yes; TLS ends at: provider
- Cost: The free tier costs nothing and needs no signup; its domains change regularly and have a speed limit.; account needed: no
- Consent text: Start a public HTTPS trial through the localhost.run relay for the requested lifetime (15 minutes by default). The relay terminates TLS and can read payloads.

## ngrok HTTPS edge

- Id: `ngrok-https-edge` (use `--route ngrok-https-edge`)
- ngrok HTTPS edge: reaches internet clients, stable address, ngrok has a $0 Free plan with one development domain, but its pricing page says custom domains need Pay-as-you-go ($20 base).
- Needs: Needs an ngrok account, its auth token and a reserved domain.
- Reach: internet; transport: https; lifetimes: attached
- Address: stable (reserved domain of your ngrok account; a reserved domain is a per-user setup value; the listener lives only while the host process runs); public ports: assigned by the provider
- Proof before publishing: checked from public; checks: tls, nonce, sse
- Traffic: readers ngrok edge; provider can read payload: yes; TLS ends at: provider
- Cost: ngrok has a $0 Free plan with one development domain, but its pricing page says custom domains need Pay-as-you-go ($20 base).; account needed: yes
- Consent text: Serve this app through an ngrok listener on your reserved ngrok domain while the app runs. The ngrok edge terminates TLS and can read payloads. The auth token stays in Gozar’s private store.
  - Terms: https://ngrok.com/tos
  - Privacy: https://ngrok.com/privacy

## ngrok TCP passthrough

- Id: `ngrok-tcp-passthrough` (use `--route ngrok-tcp-passthrough`)
- ngrok TCP passthrough: reaches internet clients, unknown address, The ngrok pricing page does not settle the cost of TCP passthrough.
- Needs: Needs an ngrok account. This route is not available in this release.
- Reach: internet; transport: http; lifetimes: none
- Address: unknown (assigned TCP address of your ngrok account; no admitted create recipe; opaque TCP: no HTTPS origin until a mapping passes a client probe); public ports: assigned by the provider
- Proof before publishing: checked from public; checks: tls, nonce, sse
- Traffic: readers the application endpoint (opaque TCP); provider can read payload: unknown; TLS ends at: unknown
- Cost: The ngrok pricing page does not settle the cost of TCP passthrough.; account needed: yes
- Consent text: ngrok TCP passthrough is detected only. Gozar cannot create a route with it yet.
  - Terms: https://ngrok.com/tos
  - Privacy: https://ngrok.com/privacy

## Your own HTTPS address

- Id: `own-address` (use `--route own-address`)
- Your own HTTPS address: reach not established, stable address, Gozar charges nothing; your own domain, hosting and certificate cost whatever you pay for them.
- Needs: Needs an HTTPS address that you run yourself and that forwards to this service.
- Reach: unknown; transport: https; lifetimes: session, durable
- Address: stable (the owner-managed origin; the owner keeps the route and the certificate; a successful response alone does not prove the correct application or outside reach); public ports: assigned by the provider
- Proof before publishing: checked from this-device; checks: tls, nonce
- Traffic: readers the owner-managed proxy; provider can read payload: unknown; TLS ends at: unknown
- Cost: Gozar charges nothing; your own domain, hosting and certificate cost whatever you pay for them.; account needed: unknown
- Consent text: Validate an existing owner-managed HTTPS origin against this instance. The address, route and certificate stay under the owner’s control; Gozar creates and deletes nothing.

## Tailscale Funnel

- Id: `tailscale-funnel` (use `--route tailscale-funnel`)
- Tailscale Funnel: reaches internet clients, stable address, Free on the Personal plan (up to 6 users); Funnel is available on all plans, with non-configurable bandwidth limits.
- Needs: Needs Tailscale installed and signed in on this computer, with Funnel allowed on your tailnet and port 8443 or 10000 free.
- Reach: internet; transport: https; lifetimes: session, durable
- Address: stable (DNS name of this node plus a port: 8443, or 10000 when 8443 is in use, for a session; the first free port of 443, 8443 and 10000 for a durable route; one of those ports must be unused and the node policy must allow it for Funnel; the tailnet administrator must allow Funnel; node and tailnet identity stay the same); public ports: 8443, 10000
- Proof before publishing: checked from public; checks: tls, nonce, sse
- Traffic: readers this device (local tailscaled); provider can read payload: no; TLS ends at: endpoint
- Cost: Free on the Personal plan (up to 6 users); Funnel is available on all plans, with non-configurable bandwidth limits.; account needed: yes
- Consent text: Publish this service over HTTPS on this device's Tailscale Funnel. A session uses port 8443, or port 10000 when 8443 is in use. A durable route uses the first free port of 443, 8443 and 10000. Existing listeners stay untouched. HTTPS, instance identity and timed SSE must pass before publication.
  - Terms: https://tailscale.com/terms
  - Privacy: https://tailscale.com/privacy-policy

## Tailscale private Serve

- Id: `tailscale-private` (use `--route tailscale-private`)
- Tailscale private Serve: reaches tailnet clients, stable address, Tailscale pricing is documented, but the Serve page does not say which plans include Serve.
- Needs: Needs Tailscale installed and signed in on this computer and port 9444 or 9445 free. Only devices on your tailnet can reach it.
- Reach: tailnet; transport: https; lifetimes: session, durable
- Address: stable (DNS name of this node plus an unused port; needs an unused Serve port; tailnet HTTPS and MagicDNS must be enabled; node and tailnet identity stay the same); public ports: 9444, 9445
- Proof before publishing: checked from tailnet; checks: tls, nonce, sse
- Traffic: readers this device (local tailscaled); provider can read payload: unknown; TLS ends at: endpoint
- Cost: Tailscale pricing is documented, but the Serve page does not say which plans include Serve.; account needed: yes
- Consent text: Publish this service over HTTPS on an unused private Tailscale Serve port of this device. Only tailnet clients can reach it. Existing listeners stay untouched.
  - Terms: https://tailscale.com/terms
  - Privacy: https://tailscale.com/privacy-policy

## tunnl.gg trial

- Id: `tunnl-gg` (use `--route tunnl-gg`)
- tunnl.gg trial: reaches internet clients, stable address, The free tier costs nothing and needs no account; Pro is $6 a month or $60 a year and removes time limits and the warning page.
- Needs: Needs the ssh command on this computer and outbound internet access. No account is needed.
- Reach: internet; transport: https; lifetimes: session
- Address: stable (address bound to an installation key; an announced address change ends the route; the relay can close quiet streams after about two minutes; browsers can show a warning page); public ports: assigned by the provider
- Proof before publishing: checked from public; checks: tls, nonce, sse
- Traffic: readers tunnl.gg relay; provider can read payload: yes; TLS ends at: provider
- Cost: The free tier costs nothing and needs no account; Pro is $6 a month or $60 a year and removes time limits and the warning page.; account needed: no
- Consent text: Start a public HTTPS trial through the tunnl.gg relay. The relay terminates TLS and can read payloads. Quiet streams can close after two minutes.
  - Terms: https://tunnl.gg/terms.md
  - Privacy: https://tunnl.gg/privacy.md
